claims: AOL.com notes that Italy has implemented a strict crackdown on citizenship by descent (jure sanguinis), severely restricting eligibility for applicants with distant Italian ancestry.
ETIAS.com says effective March 2025, citizenship is generally limited to those with a parent or grandparent born in Italy.
ETIAS.com says citizenship often requires proof the ancestor never naturalized elsewhere.
ETIAS.com says the changes effectively end claims through great-grandparents.
Citizenship is mostly limited to children and grandchildren of Italian-born ancestors.
New rules state that if an Italian ancestor naturalized while their child was still a minor, the line of citizenship is broken.
New rules are supported by recent court rulings.
Starting in 2029, all applications must be filed with a central office in Rome, reports this YouTube video.
Applicants must prove "true interest" in Italy, notes AOL.com.
Applicants face stricter scrutiny of documentation, notes AOL.com.
The restrictions generally do not apply to cases filed before the new, tighter regulations, says this YouTube video.
The restrictions generally do not apply to specific 1948 cases, says this YouTube video.
The crackdown has been upheld by the Italian Constitutional Court, according to this Threads post and IMI Daily.
